annotations.text:
Order, top to bottom, follows the work
Gear (what kind, one or two) · Pair (solve it: this fills the gears, so it comes before them; its Candidates button moves up here from the SolidWorks bar) · Gear A and Gear B (type or adjust) · Derived (what that comes to) · Output · SolidWorks · Build.
Today Pair sits under Derived, so a pair is solved by going down, then back up, then down again.

What the numbers mean, as you type
One card at the foot of the gear panel follows the caret: the field's name and symbol, two sentences on what it is, and the typed value worked out — m 1.5 × z 20 = PD 30 mm. The Tk field already knows when it has focus; the card swaps its text on that.
The third artboard has every card's copy and diagram.

Derived, in pair mode
Both gears drawn at one scale, meshed at the centre distance their teeth make, the pitch circles dashed and touching at the pitch point. The centre distance is dimensioned below; a single gear gets its pitch diameter the same way. The values sit under it in two columns, with the pair's own three above them.
